Class MarkdownView

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.markdown.MarkdownView
All Implemented Interfaces:
Widget
public final class MarkdownView extends Object implements Widget
A widget that renders CommonMark + GFM markdown to a Buffer.

Robustness against partial input is built in: before every parse the source is run through a sanitizer that trims trailing unmatched inline markers (**, _, ~, `) and dangling links. Well-formed markdown is returned unchanged. As a result, a consumer can re-bind the source on every render — for example, to display a markdown stream produced by an LLM — without flicker or stray markers showing up.

CSS Properties

Same single-resolver pattern as Block: properties have flat names resolved against one StylePropertyResolver that the caller has already scoped to this widget. Each markdown sub-element exposes three properties built from the standard ColorConverter and ModifierConverter:
  • <element>-color — foreground color
  • <element>-background — background color
  • <element>-text-style — modifier set
where <element> is one of heading-1 … heading-6, strong, emphasis, strikethrough, inline-code, code-block, link, blockquote, list-marker, html, horizontal-rule, task-checked, or task-unchecked.

Plus a few string properties that mirror the Checkbox widget convention:

  • BLOCKQUOTE_PREFIX (blockquote-prefix) — leading bar glyph drawn at the start of each quoted line; a single space is always appended after it.
  • TASK_CHECKED_SYMBOL (task-checked-symbol) and TASK_UNCHECKED_SYMBOL (task-unchecked-symbol) — glyphs drawn for GFM task-list items; defaults are [x] and [ ], again followed by a single space.

And the widget-wide text-overflow property (StandardProperties.TEXT_OVERFLOW) controlling how prose lines wider than the content area are handled.

Programmatic MarkdownStyles overrides take priority; unset slots fall back to CSS, then to built-in defaults.

Example TCSS (the type selector matches whatever style type the caller has assigned to this widget): 

MarkdownView {
    heading-1-color: magenta;
    heading-1-text-style: bold;
    link-color: green;
    link-text-style: underlined;
    blockquote-color: yellow;
    blockquote-background: black;
    blockquote-prefix: "> ";
}

Supported markdown elements:

  • Headings (1-6) with bold styling and an underline rule for H1/H2
  • Paragraphs with width-aware word wrap
  • Bullet, ordered, and task (GFM) lists with nested indentation
  • Block quotes (single bar, dim style)
  • Fenced and indented code blocks (rounded Block border, info string used as title)
  • GFM tables (delegated to Table)
  • Inline emphasis, strong, strikethrough, code, and links (links use the OSC-8 hyperlink extension)
  • Thematic breaks rendered as a horizontal rule
  • HTML blocks and inline HTML rendered as dim escaped text
  • Images rendered as [image: alt](url) text spans

    • computeHeight

      public int computeHeight(int width)
      Computes the total number of rows the rendered markdown would take at width columns. Outer Block chrome (borders, padding, titles) is included if a block has been set. Useful for size-aware layout containers that need to know how tall the widget wants to be given an available width.
      Parameters:
      width - the available width in columns
      Returns:
      total rows needed; 0 when width <= 0
